memory_candidates.content: When a fidelity/provenance audit script's --write mode operates over an entire corpus rather than a single targeted document (no per-document CLI selector), re-running it to re-adjudicate one document can incidentally recompute ratios for unrelated entries due to extractor non-determinism (e.g. pdftotext whitespace/ordering variance across runs). This is not a bug in the audit logic itself but a side effect of full-corpus recomputation. When diffing before/after snapshots to verify a targeted re-adjudication, expect and explicitly account for this class of incidental drift rather than treating any non-target change as a scope violation.

A quarantine-list-based fail-open design (values NOT in QUARANTINED_FIDELITY_VALUES are citable by default) can silently reverse polarity when an external, unversioned data repository (here, a separate ~/Projects/Literature git repo tracking index.json) introduces a new stamped value that was always in the code's enum but never previously populated at scale. The code itself did not change and no one edited the quarantine constant, yet the population of documents treated as citable-by-default grew ~7x. When auditing fidelity/quarantine systems, always re-measure the live population size against a stamped value rather than trusting an earlier report's count, since population drift can happen entirely outside the audited repository's own commits.
